solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cryptic clue brains need time to unravel

indicators.note: unravelling a knot of letters means teasing them apart into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A puzzle clue that takes thinking time to work out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic clue' reads as one phrase, but only 'Cryptic' is the definition; CLUE, BRAINS and T are mixed together by 'to unravel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something mysterious whose meaning is hard to read.

clue.text: Having a ball, including one's sweetheart

parts.note: INC is the short form of including
a sweetheart is a lover

explanation.surface: Someone is having a great time with their sweetheart along.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms mean enjoying oneself in great comfort and luck.

clue.text: Swingeing fines involving the pub party

indicators.note: the remade letters wrap around the pub
swingeing suggests a violent swing, so the letters of fines are knocked about

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Heavy fines are imposed on a political party over a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swingeing' (severe) looks like it describes the fines, but it is the anagram signal. Sinn Fein is an Irish political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinn Fein is an Irish political party, so an example.

clue.text: Remove part of bird's crest

indicators.note: taking away means a piece is cut from the bird

parts.note: a partridge is a game bird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird keeper trims away part of the bird's crest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird's crest' reads as feathers, but crest stands alone as the definition: a hilltop or ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is the crest or top line of a hill.

clue.text: Have a chocolaty snack, perhaps, to beat everything

definitions.meaning: taking a ..., chocolate-coated perhaps, from the plate
an idiom for being the most outrageous of all

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, accepting a snack; idiomatically, being the most remarkable or outrageous thing.

clue.text: A little bird, a bigger bird

parts.note: a bit is a small amount
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A list comparing a small bird with a larger one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bittern is a heron-like marsh bird, larger than a tern.

clue.text: African piano, the one that's playing

indicators.note: playing about with letters shuffles them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An African musician performs on the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks like playing music, but it shuffles PIANO, THE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Ethiopia, a country in Africa, so an African.

clue.text: Pull heads off tulips or wallflowers

indicators.note: the heads of the three words are their first letters, taken off and used

explanation.surface: A gardener drags the flower heads off the plants.
explanation.definitionFit: To tow a vehicle is to pull it along behind.

clue.text: Game of numbers, including 15, oddly

indicators.note: the plural word holds the picked letters within it

parts.note: tens are numbers

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters, first and third, of the answer to 15 are taken

parts.note: refers to the answer to 15 across, NAIL

explanation.surface: A sport scored in odd numbers, starting strangely at fifteen.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' looks like the tennis score, but it points to the answer at 15 across; 'oddly' takes N and I from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, so an example of a game.

clue.text: Drawback taking exercise? It gets you out of shape!

indicators.note: one word takes another into its middle

parts.note: draw, written back to front, gives the word for a hospital room
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: The downside of a workout is that it bends you out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawback' looks like a disadvantage, but it tells you to write DRAW backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Warped means bent or twisted, no longer in its proper form.

clue.text: Drunk, withholding name, may be punished

indicators.note: holding back a letter means it is taken out of the word for drunk

parts.note: canned is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk who will not give their name may face punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caned was a schoolroom punishment with a stick.

clue.text: Room the Queen gives the field marshal

parts.note: a kitchen is a room in a house
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: The monarch grants a room to a senior army officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener was a famous British field marshal of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchener held the top British army rank of field marshal.

clue.text: It's eccentric of Crux to keep frogs, primarily

indicators.note: one piece keeps another held within its letters

parts.note: taken as written
the crux of a matter is its centre; Crux is also the setter's pseudonym

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the word frogs

explanation.surface: The setter Crux seems odd for keeping pet frogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crux' looks like the setter naming themself, but here it means the heart or centre of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something not quite in the middle, literally or in behaviour.

clue.text: Female duck not recorded

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, written like the letter O
a live performance is broadcast as it happens, not recorded

explanation.surface: A female duck that was never caught on tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female duck' reads as one bird; the definition is just 'Female', for a woman's given name.
explanation.definitionFit: A given name for a girl or woman, so a female example.

clue.text: Chapter of endless saga does, in translation

indicators.note: the long story loses its final letter

parts.note: an epic is a long heroic story, like a saga

indicators.note: translating rewrites words, so the letters of does are rearranged

explanation.surface: Translating a never-ending saga into another language takes a chapter at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' turns EPIC into EPI, and 'in translation' rearranges DOES into SODE.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is one instalment of a longer story, like a chapter.

clue.text: 20% like Pinky, for instance

definitions.meaning: the pinky is one finger of a hand of five

explanation.definitionFit: Twenty per cent is a fifth; the little finger is one of a hand's five.

clue.text: Brad, say, last in cabin to go sick

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word cabin is used

parts.note: to ail is to fall ill

explanation.surface: Brad is the final person in the cabin to fall ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brad' looks like a man's name, but a brad is a small thin nail.
explanation.definitionFit: A brad is a type of small slim nail, so an example.

clue.text: Cold weather headgear, apparently, much reduced

definitions.text: Cold weather headgear, apparently, much reduced

parts.words: Cold weather headgear, apparently, much reduced
parts.note: a hat for icy weather on the face of it, but really the ice at the poles, shrinking with warming

explanation.surface: A warm winter hat is on sale at a big discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much reduced' reads as a sale price, but refers to melting ice sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: The ice covering a planet's poles, which has shrunk greatly in recent decades.

clue.text: Use drugs? He'd have a job!

parts.note: to employ something is to use it
E is slang for ecstasy, so two Es are drugs

explanation.surface: Taking drugs on the job would get a worker into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker with a job is someone employed by another.

clue.text: Part of speech dropped nowadays, for another

indicators.note: a short piece is let fall out of another part of speech

parts.note: another part of speech here is an adverb
AD (anno Domini) marks the present era, so nowadays

explanation.surface: A grammar term that has fallen out of use today, replaced by another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points back to 'Part of speech': a different part of speech, ADVERB.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb is a word class, one of the grammatical categories.

clue.text: See 4
Run with the pack, like Tory at his best

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party
someone at their best is said to be on form

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician is happiest following the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to follow the group, behaving as others do.

clue.text: Nearly finish working

parts.note: to close something is to finish it
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A job is almost done.
explanation.definitionFit: Close on means nearly or almost, as in close on midnight.

clue.text: Yet Man, pace Donne, really is one!

definitions.text: Yet Man, pace Donne, really is one!

parts.words: Yet Man, pace Donne, really is one!
parts.note: John Donne wrote that no man is one, but the Isle of Man is a piece of land in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Contradicting the poet Donne, a man truly can stand alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pace' is Latin for 'with due respect to'. Donne's poem says 'No man is an island'; the Isle of Man is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is land surrounded by sea in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: US city leader, short and overweight

indicators.note: a short version loses its last letter

parts.note: a boss is a leader
a ton is a heavy weight, slang for too much

explanation.surface: An American mayor is described as brief and overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Boston is a city in Massachusetts, so an example.

clue.text: Faint circle in fresh snow

indicators.note: the round letter sits inside the remade word
a fresh version of the word snow is a new arrangement of its letters

parts.note: the letter O is round like a circle

explanation.surface: Someone sees a ring in newly fallen snow, only faintly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to pass out briefly, losing consciousness.

clue.text: Hold up progress, partly thanks to new alliance

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Progress is being held back, partly because of a new political alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to obstruct or delay by refusing to cooperate.

clue.text: More like one of the crowd

definitions.meaning: a film ... appears in crowd scenes

explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional; an extra is a background actor in a crowd scene.

clue.text: Quality credit

definitions.meaning: a characteristic or feature something has
to credit something to someone is to ascribe it to them

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a quality; as a verb it means to credit or ascribe.

clue.text: Tasteless play ends after short 15

indicators.note: the final letter follows the short nail

parts.note: 15 is the answer NAIL; a short nail is a tack

indicators.note: the end of the word play is its last letter

explanation.surface: A vulgar play finishes after a brief run.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacky describes something cheap and vulgar, showing poor taste.

clue.text: Press for payment to be completed, we hear

indicators.note: says the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: something completed is done

explanation.surface: A debt collector demands payment to settle the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To dun a debtor is to keep demanding they pay up.

clue.text: Could be Jonathan's original sin

parts.note: Jonathan is a variety of apple, and the original sin in Eden was tasting the forbidden fruit

explanation.surface: Someone named Jonathan committed the first sin of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jonathan' looks like a person, but it is a dessert apple variety; Eve's original sin was biting the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert apple for raw eating, as opposed to a cooking apple, of which Jonathan is one.
